summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on embedded firmware experience across STM32, Arduino, and Raspberry Pi platforms. Wrote embedded C to drive multi-servo PWM control and read distance and accelerometer sensors in real time, and built bare-metal drivers for GPIO, ADC, I2C, and UART peripherals. Comfortable debugging physical hardware with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, and scripting test and automation tooling in Python.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python scripting.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented embedded C sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Wrote embedded C to implement multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override on STM32.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF distance sensing with OLED visualization.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal embedded C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 hardware integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) during physical system bring-up and hardware-in-the-loop testing; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection using dual VL53L0X ToF sensors.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
